author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Hand-built functional-test states in the tool-neutral vocabulary of SPEC-functionaltest §13 (rev 2026-09-22.1): the four spec presets (2oo3 SIL 2 trip, five-point loop checks, transfer sequence with retest, trip setpoint revised after FAT), voting-degradation enumeration for 1oo1, 1oo2, 2oo2, 2oo3, 4oo8 and 2oo9 at every coverage level, staleness by FNV-1a hash of the model slice (including the §4.4 worked hashes and the acceptance-4/5 scope of staleness), five-point AI/AO loop arithmetic with boundary cases, DI/DO state checks, SIL proof-test completeness, bypass/force restoration, execution-record rules, package flags, scope exclusion, coverage figures and the §6 verdict. Every reference value was computed by functionaltest-ref.py, an independent standard-library re-implementation of the spec written without the tool code, and asserted against a hand-derived expectation per check. Phase vocabulary and test purpose follow IEC 62381:2024 (FAT/FIT/SAT/SIT), IEC 62382:2024 (loop check between loop construction and cold commissioning, documented per cl. 7) and IEC 61511-1:2016 cl. 15 (SIS safety validation against the SRS); the five-point injection, tolerance rule, voting combinations, bypass-restoration and proof-test predicates are the spec's author method.
reference_citations: IEC 62382:2024 Ed. 3.0 'Control systems in the process industry - Electrical and instrumentation loop check', preview sample https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/104569/954e455763a94f98b5f16dce4ef31098/IEC-62382-2024.pdf - 1.1 scope, 3.1.15 loop, clause titles 4-10 incl. 7 'Documentation of performed loop checks' (read 2026-09-22)

IEC 62381:2024 Ed. 3.0 'Automation systems in the process industry - FAT, SAT and SIT', webstore listing and preview sample as cited in spec §0 (clauses 5-8, 3.1.16 punch list); not re-read beyond the spec's quotation

IEC 61511-1:2016 cl. 15 SIS safety validation, 15.1.1 objective as quoted by Emerson Automation Experts 'Safety Validation in the IEC 61511 Process Safety Lifecycle' (2010) https://www.emersonautomationexperts.com/2010/safety/safety_validati/ (read 2026-09-22); the standard's 15.2 item list was not read
FNV-1a 32-bit parameters (offset basis 2166136261, prime 16777619) and check vectors '' -> 811c9dc5, 'a' -> e40c292c as given in spec §4.4
tolerance: Categorical, boolean, integer, id-list and hash checks are exact (discrete logic; any deviation is a logic difference). `test.<id>.expected` is compared as canonical JSON (spec §4.4). Coverage percentages are one IEEE division: relative 1e-12. Loop expected values, deviations and signals are at most three IEEE operations in the spec's expression order: relative 1e-12, and absolute 1e-9·S (S = span) where the reference is exactly 0, as spec §13.2 states. Every `within` check keeps ||d| - t| > 1e-6·S so no floating boundary decides it; the exact-equality boundary |d| = t is checked only through rule_absent.
not_benchmarked: Step, precondition, label and expected_text wording, and the seven-language UI (spec §14).
UI behaviour: conflict table, filters, figures, mobile layout, permalink size fallback, PDF layout (spec §14).
Package transport (explicit load, round trip, ignored-field report, atomic refusal of save while FUN-R-007 fires) and §7.2 field aliases: package cases per TZ-project-package §7, not this corpus.
'Refresh from model' and idempotent re-generation (acceptance 3 and 9): actions on a state, not expressible in the §13.1 input vocabulary.
Display-unit conversions (§4.8) and the 0-10V signal value (§13.2 names only signal_A).
Generation-refusal input limits of §2 (20 matrices, 2 000 cells, 5 000 tests ...): no case exceeds them except n = 9 channels, see vote-n9-single.
Segment classes of Figure 1 (valid_pass / fail / invalid_pass / deferred / not_tested / no_test): not a §13.2 checkable key.
Hashes of strings outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (spec §14).
The content of IEC 61511-1:2016 15.2 and IEC 62382 test-point percentages or tolerances: not read (spec §0); the corresponding rules are the spec's author method.
coverage: 128 cases (113 authored + 4 added by the first adjudication 2026-09-23 + 11 added by the second adjudication 2026-09-23). Rules with a triggering case: 34 of 34 (all). Rules with a near-miss case where they do not fire: 34 of 34 (all). Headline claims: presets P1-P4 with spec §9 findings, coverage and verdicts; §4.4 worked hashes; acceptance 4 (setpoint change stales exactly the cause's tests), 5 (non-slice edits stale nothing), 7 (boundaries |d| = t and tolerance = accuracy), 8 (voting counts 0/3/6/7, 255 at n = 8, FUN-R-008 at n = 9). Added by the first adjudication: §5.5 loop span taken from the range recorded in the test after a model change, §5.3 hidden test of an excluded category firing nothing, §4.3 unconditional reset step of a generated sif_proof, §5.5 suppression of FUN-R-042 while FUN-R-043 fires. Added by the second adjudication: the §4.7 valid-pass list against a pass that fires FUN-R-043, the §4.5 required checkpoint set (short list, empty list), the loop rules that read the point and not the stored expected (FUN-R-041, -043, -044), FUN-R-043 without an upper tolerance bound, the control_function branch of FUN-R-052, the effects[].tag branch of FUN-R-004, the coverage denominator of two sources sharing one key (transitions and io), and the 'one finding per (rule, target)' sentence of §5.

cases.intent: spec §4.3: the generated sif_proof carries a reset step even when the cause reset mode is none, so FUN-R-015 does not fire
cases.notes: added by adjudication: every FUN-R-015 near miss in the corpus used reset 'manual'; the conditional reset of ce_cell and voting does not apply to sif_proof.

generated_ids.derivation: spec §4.3 step table: the sif_proof step list is 'check; inject on every channel (all n); observe each trip-effect tag; reset cause tag; check' with no condition on the cause reset mode, unlike ce_cell ('reset cause tag when cell type is trip and reset != none') and voting. So a SIL cause with reset 'none' still gets a proof test carrying a reset step and is complete under §5.2 (c), and FUN-R-015 does not fire. n = 1 gives no voting source (§4.1 requires n >= 2). Sources: 1 cell + 1 sif = 2, none covered because both tests are not_tested, so §6 gives open with no finding.

patch.actual: Readings match at every point; the loop was rejected for cable screening

rule_targets.FUN-R-043.derivation: spec §5.5 closing sentence: 'When FUN-R-043 fires, FUN-R-040 and FUN-R-042 are not evaluated for that test.' The AI loop test has tolerance_pct null, so FUN-R-043 fires (major); the result is fail with every point recorded and equal to the expected value, which would otherwise be the FUN-R-042 trigger, and FUN-R-042 must stay silent. FUN-R-044 needs tolerance_pct > 0. The punch reference closes FUN-R-031. S = 1 000 000 Pa, x_50 = 500 000 Pa, d_50 = 0. Ma = 1 -> verdict open; the failure is executed but not covering.

cases.intent: FUN-R-043 has no upper bound: a loop tolerance of 15 % of span is finite and above 0, so the rule stays silent
cases.notes: added by adjudication: the corpus pinned FUN-R-043 at 0 and null only, so a tool that also treated a tolerance above the 10 % of settings.default_tolerance_pct as invalid was not caught.

generated_ids.derivation: spec §5.5 trigger: FUN-R-043 fires on kind = loop and an AI/AO point when not (isFinite(tolerance_pct) and tolerance_pct > 0). 15 is finite and above 0, so the rule is silent; the '> 0, <= 10' domain of §3.1 binds settings.default_tolerance_pct, the source of the generated value, and §3.5 puts no domain on tests[].tolerance_pct. FUN-R-044 needs an io_accuracy entry above 0 and there is none. §5.6: scope.ce false excludes cells and voting, scope.sequences false excludes transitions and mode edges, so FUN-R-060 fires four times (info). §4.7: the one io source is not covered (the test is not_tested), so §6 gives open with B = Ma = Mi = 0.

cases.intent: spec §4.7: a passed loop check whose tolerance is null is still a valid pass, because FUN-R-043 is not in the valid-pass exclusion list
cases.notes: added by adjudication: §4.7 lists exactly FUN-R-022, -030, -040, -041 and -050; no case pinned the coverage figure of a pass that fires FUN-R-043, so a sixth exclusion in the tool went unseen.

rule_present.FUN-R-043.derivation: spec §4.7: 'A test is a valid pass <=> result = pass and not stale and none of FUN-R-022, FUN-R-030, FUN-R-040, FUN-R-041, FUN-R-050 fires on it.' The list is closed and FUN-R-043 is not in it. Here result = pass, the model_hash is the current one (not stale), evidence_ref is set (no FUN-R-030), every one of the five points is recorded (no FUN-R-041), no step bypasses anything (no FUN-R-050) and the expected object is the generated one (no FUN-R-022). FUN-R-040 and FUN-R-042 are not evaluated at all, because §5.5 suppresses them while FUN-R-043 fires. So the test is a valid pass, the io source is covered 1 of 1 and the only finding is the FUN-R-043 major, which by §6 (B = 0, Ma = 1) gives open.

cases.intent: spec §5: two dangling transitions sharing a key give one FUN-R-005 finding, not one per transition
cases.notes: added by adjudication: the 'one finding per (rule, target)' sentence that opens §5 had no case, and a tool pushing one finding per model row inflates every severity count.

generated_ids.derivation: spec §5 opens with 'One finding per (rule, target)'. Both transitions of FN-3 name the non-existent step SX and both carry the id T9, so FUN-R-005's target, the transition key FN-3|T9, is the same for both and the major fires once. §5.1: FUN-R-005 means no test is generated, and §4.1 keeps a transition out of the source set unless its 'to' exists, so the transitions category has no source at all. §5.6 adds FUN-R-060 for cells, voting and io. §6 is evaluated top down and the first row matches: total over the six categories is 0 and tests is empty -> empty, ahead of the major.

adjudication: Adjudication pass 2026-09-23 against SPEC-functionaltest rev 2026-09-22.1 as amended on 2026-09-23 (spec §17 changelog): four cases added (each marked in its notes), no case corrected, none removed. The §13.2 readings of hash.<test id>, test.<id>.expected and loop.<test id>.* were under-specified; the spec now states they are the values stored on the test, which is the reading this corpus already used. Second adjudication pass 2026-09-23 (differential audit of the build against an independent re-implementation, 250 random states): 11 cases added, each marked in its notes, no case corrected, none removed. Spec §4.5 and §5.5 were amended (spec §17 changelog) to fix the required checkpoint set of a loop test and to state which loop rules survive a stored expected that carries no point list; six tool defects follow from the spec as it already stood and are listed in ADJUDICATION.md.
